title: An arrow tip lands on the edge it is pointing at
goal: When you point an arrow at something in a screenshot, the tip should land on that edge rather than a couple of pixels short of it. At the size a Retina capture opens at, one step of the mouse moves the tip two pixels, so hitting an edge by eye is luck. The arrow should magnetize to the edges the app has already found, exactly the way a measurement caliper does.
notes: Raised on 2026-09-05 while auditing the captioned-arrow fixes. The user reported the tail stopping a few pixels short of what it points at; measured, the tip lands exactly on the endpoint at every zoom, pixel scale, stroke width and head scale, so the geometry is right and the AIM is what is short. At 100% on a pixelScale 2 capture, viewport zoom is 0.5, so one pointer point is two image pixels. EdgeSnapping already exists and MeasureHandleDrag uses it (CanvasView around line 2020, axisGated + EdgeSnapping.snap with the edgeMap); annotation endpoint drags and the create drag apply no snapping at all. Reuse the same call, the same guide layer, and the same modifier gate.
acceptance: Dragging an arrow so its tip nears a detected edge snaps the tip onto that edge, with the same yellow guide a caliper shows
The snap can be refused: holding a modifier, or moving further away, leaves the tip exactly where the pointer is
The same snap works on the tail end and when dragging either end of an existing arrow
A picture at 4x shows the tip landing on the edge with no gap, taken by eye rather than by typed coordinates

log.note: Adversarial review before building. The mock/task says 'reuse the caliper's call'. Two things in it are wrong for an arrow. (1) The caliper's axis gate reads the direction the HAND is travelling; an arrow's aim is a steadier and truer signal, so the gate reads the SHAFT: a flat arrow takes only the vertical border ahead of it and keeps the height you chose along it, an upright one only the horizontal edge, a diagonal one both so it can land in a corner. (2) The caliper's guide lines (other measurements) and centre snapping have no business deciding where an arrow points, so annotations catch detected edges and the pixel grid only. Shortest version that delivers the value: one pure helper, called from three places.

Built: PhotonzCore/AnnotationSnapping.swift (16 tests, written first) + wired into CanvasView's create-drag anchor, create-drag move and endpoint-drag move. EditorState.snappingEdgeMap now also runs for drawing tools and for a selected line/arrow, so picking the Arrow tool starts the edge sweep. The yellow guide survives the select-only chrome guard so it shows while a mark is being drawn.

Adversarial review of the BUILT thing, on the probe. First run found the fix defeating itself: SnapHold keeps a caught line until the pointer is twice the magnet's reach away, which is right for a short caliper adjustment but wrong for a mark that sweeps across the picture. An upright arrow aimed 3px over a button's top edge (755) parked on the button label's cap top (776) picked up on the way, 24px short of the aim - the very complaint the task is about. Fixed in AnnotationSnapping: a held line that is farther from the pointer than a line the pointer can reach by itself is treated as left behind. Re-run: the tip lands on 755. Every drag still reports 'went back on themselves 0', so no flicker was traded for it.

Verified in Photonz Probe with Scripts/playtest/arrow-tip-snap-walk.json on the settings-pane-2x fixture (Save Changes button detected at x 233..481, y 755..816). Flat arrow aimed at 484 lands on 481, keeping y. Upright arrow aimed at 752 lands on 755, keeping x. Diagonal arrow lands on the corner (232, 816). The same arrow's TIP and TAIL handles snap when re-dragged. Command holds the tip at 484 exactly; Shift does too, because the 45 degree constraint owns the point. A rectangle dragged loosely round the button comes out (232, 755, 249, 61), which is the button. 4x renders cropped at each tip show no gap; corner-guide-sc.png is a real screen capture of the crossed yellow guides mid-drag.

Arrow, line and box endpoints magnetize to the picture's detected borders with the caliper's yellow guide. New PhotonzCore/AnnotationSnapping (16 tests, written first) gated by the direction the MARK points, not the hand; wired into the create-drag anchor, the create-drag move and the endpoint-drag move; snappingEdgeMap now runs for drawing tools too. Also fixed the magnet defeating itself: a line caught mid-sweep used to ride along and park the tip 24px short of the aim. Verified in the probe with Scripts/playtest/arrow-tip-snap-walk.json (tips land on 481 / 755 / the corner 232,816; tip and tail handles snap; Command and Shift refuse; a loose rectangle comes out hugging the button; zero guides going back on themselves) plus 13 related walks green and Scripts/test.sh at 3611. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-05-arrow-tip-snap.json. Commit 3cc3f8f, pushed.
